intro.text: 48 lessons cover testing, functional and structural techniques, unit testing, pytest, TDD, integration and system testing. Follow them with the mini revision questions and practice problems.

blocks.text: Even simple errors such as integer overflow can crash entire systems. Airport system failures and spacecraft crashes show why software testing matters.
Reflection: how have you tested a program you wrote?
Integer overflow, an airport system failure and a spacecraft crash illustrate the consequences of software errors.

sections.title: Building the Right Thing vs Building It Right

blocks.text: Earlier weeks focused on finding the right requirements and communicating with clients: building the right thing.
This week focuses on building it right: testing that modules are built correctly.

blocks.caption: Building the Right Thing vs Building It Right
blocks.alt: Building the Right Thing vs Building It Right

blocks.text: Provide inputs; check the output; see whether it matches expectations; locate the error; identify its cause; fix the error; test again. These activities connect testing with debugging.
A test case is the triplet [I, S, R]. I is the data input to the program; S is the state of the program at which that data is input; R is the expected result.

Seller portal: after login, the user is on the catalog page, clicks “add item to the catalog” and fills the details (S). The item details are the input (I). The expected result is that the catalog page displays the new item (R).
A test suite is the set of all test cases designed to test a given program.

The activities are test suite design; running test cases and checking results; locating the error; and error correction. A mismatch indicates a failure. The tester notes and reports it to the developer, who is often the same person.
Random tests do not guarantee that most errors will be found. Consider the faulty minimum calculation: if (x < y) min = x; else min = x.
Pairs (1, 2), (3, 4) and (1000, 10000) all pass because x is smaller. Design cases where the first value is minimum, the second value is minimum, and both values are equal.
The input domain is too large to test exhaustively. Design a minimal test suite in which each test case detects a different type of error.
Unit testing tests individual functions or units. Integration testing incrementally combines units and tests them after each step.
System testing tests the fully integrated system. Alpha testing is performed by the test team within the organisation; beta testing involves a select group of customers.
In acceptance testing, the customer checks the requirements or user stories and decides whether to accept delivery. Performance testing checks non-functional requirements.
Unit testing checks an individual unit. Integration testing detects errors at module interfaces, including parameter passing and communication between modules.
Alpha testing is performed by the test team within the organisation. Beta testing is performed by a select group of customers on the fully integrated system.
The customer checks whether the system meets the requirements or user stories and decides whether to accept delivery.

Black-box testing is also called functional testing. Treat the program as a black box and design tests by examining input and output values, with no knowledge of its design or code. For example, test the values returned by min(x, y).
Partition the input domain into equivalence classes: the program behaves similarly for every input in a class. Select one representative from each class.
For min(x, y), the classes are x > y (for example (20, 10) or (50, 40)), x < y, and x = y.
For x < y, min(3, 8) returns 3. For x > y, min(9, 4) returns 4. For x = y, min(5, 5) returns 5. Each pair represents one equivalence class.

isPrime(num) takes a positive integer. Its equivalence classes are prime numbers, which should return True, and non-prime numbers, which should return False. Choose one representative from each class.
Programmers may confuse for i in range(n) with range(n-1), or < with <=. Examine values at the boundaries of equivalence classes. For isPrime(num), check 0 and 1.
For isPrime(num), 0 and 1 are boundary values and are not prime. The values 2 and 3 are prime.

From requirements or specifications, identify input and output structures and values. Identify equivalence classes. Choose one representative test case from each class. Design boundary-value test cases.
White-box testing is also called structural testing. Analyse the structure of the program using heuristics such as coverage. Test coverage checks that paths through the program are covered.
Black-box testing is functional testing: use input and output values. White-box testing is structural testing: examine the program structure to design tests.
Branch coverage requires every branch to be taken at least once. For min(x, y), one test has x < y and another has x >= y.

sections.title: Testing Both Branches of min(x, y)

blocks.text: With (3, 8), x < y is True and the result is 3. With (9, 4), x < y is False and the result is 4.

blocks.caption: Testing Both Branches of min(x, y)
blocks.alt: Testing Both Branches of min(x, y)

blocks.text: The test suite {0, 2, 3, 4} guarantees branch coverage for the lecture’s isPrime code.
0 takes the True guard branch; 2 does not enter the loop; 3 is prime and its remainder test is never zero; 4 takes the num % i == 0 branch.
In multiple condition coverage, each component of a composite condition takes True and False values. For num == 0 or num == 1, the inputs {0, 1} achieve multiple condition coverage.

For if (num < 50 || num > 150), {49, 100} achieves branch coverage. The set {49, 100, 200} achieves multiple condition coverage. Multiple condition coverage can therefore be stronger than branch coverage.

In a control-flow graph, nodes represent line numbers and an edge means control flows from one line to another. For path coverage, the test suite accesses all linearly independent paths at least once.
The lecture’s independent paths are {1, 2, 3} for 0 or 1; {1, 2, 4, 7} for 2; {1, 2, 4, 5, 6} for the non-prime 4; and {1, 2, 4, 5, 4, 7} for the prime 3.
Cyclomatic complexity is the number of decision and loop statements plus 1. Here it is 3 + 1 = 4: four independent paths, requiring at least four test cases.
Other modules may not be ready when a module is written. Testing a unit separately also makes debugging easier because the module containing the error is easier to identify.
WHEN: during coding of the module, rather than waiting for the testing phase. WHO: the person writing the code. WHAT: design unit test cases and a testing environment.
The module under test may access non-local data and call functions that are not yet available, such as function_1, function_2 and function_3.

A driver contains the non-local data structures accessed by the module under test. A stub is a dummy procedure with the same input/output parameters as the called function and highly simplified behaviour.
A stub is a dummy procedure with the same input/output parameters as the function the module calls, with highly simplified behaviour.
In the demo, get_total_items is not yet implemented by another developer. Define mock_get_total_items to sum seller_inventory_map and use a mock with side_effect=mock_get_total_items in the test.
A driver contains the non-local data structures accessed by the module under test and calls the module. A stub stands in for a function that the module calls.
unittest is part of Python’s built-in standard library. pytest is popular and minimises boilerplate code. Install it with pip install pytest and run tests with pytest.
The lecture names test files with the test_ prefix, such as test_seller_portal.py, and test functions with the test_ prefix. Without those prefixes in the demo, pytest reports no tests run.
Example: def test_double(): assert double(10) == 20.
An assertion checks a condition: assert actual == expected. If the comparison is False, Python raises AssertionError.

The lecture uses a Product class and a SellerInventory class. seller_inventory_map stores {product_id: count}. add_items_to_inventory adds items, delete_items removes them and raises an exception if the requested number exceeds availability. get_total_items is not yet implemented.
Add 10 items of product P1: seller_inventory_map[P1] is 10. Add 10 more: the expected count is 20.

sections.title: A Unit Test Catches a Bug

blocks.text: Forgetting the + replaces the count instead of adding to it. The second addition produces 10 instead of 20, causing AssertionError: 10 != 20. Fix the addition and all tests pass.

blocks.caption: A Unit Test Catches a Bug
blocks.alt: A Unit Test Catches a Bug

blocks.text: Add 10 items and delete 5. The expected remaining count is 5.
A fixture method such as inventory() initialises the object once for use in all test cases in the lecture example.
Add 10 items and attempt to delete 20. A test using pytest.raises(ValueError) passes when ValueError is raised. If the test deletes only 5, the expected exception is not raised and that test fails.

Traditionally, tests are written after the code. Test-driven development, used especially in Agile, writes tests first and drives design and development from them, iterating over small sub-functionalities.
RED: express the requirement as a test, run it and see it fail. GREEN: write the minimum code needed to pass. REFACTOR: make the code modular and elegant while the tests still pass. Repeat.
First test a non-prime such as 4: expect False. The test fails; add a loop that returns False when num % i == 0, then it passes.
Next test is_prime(5): expect True. It fails; add return True and it passes. The test for 2 already passes.
The test for 1 fails; add if num == 1: return False. The test for 0 fails next; add the 0 check. Develop one small test at a time.
The important cases are is_prime(5) → True, is_prime(4) → False, is_prime(2) → True, is_prime(1) → False and is_prime(0) → False.
Integration testing

Begin integration testing when a few or all modules have been unit-tested. The objective is to detect interface errors such as parameter passing and communication errors. In the lecture example, M1 calls M2, M3 and M4, with M5 below.
Big bang
In big bang integration, integrate all modules in one step. Errors are hard to localise. This is meaningful only for small systems, never for large systems.
Bottom up
In bottom up integration, integrate each subsystem first: M1, M2 and M3 form one subsystem, and M4 and M5 another. Then combine them. No stubs are needed; drivers simulate the global variables.
Top down
In top down integration, start with the root and one or two subordinate modules, then proceed to the next level: M1 → M2, M3, M4 → M5. No drivers are needed; stubs stand in for modules such as M5.
Mixed integration
Combine bottom up and top down integration as modules become available after unit testing.
System testing

Test the fully integrated system. Alpha testing uses the organisation’s test team; beta testing uses selected customers; acceptance testing lets the customer check requirements or user stories and decide whether to accept delivery.
Smoke testing
Before initial system testing, including alpha or beta, smoke testing runs a few basic cases to check basic functionality, such as adding products to the catalogue or inventory.
Performance and stress testing

Performance testing checks non-functional requirements. Stress testing is a type of performance testing that goes beyond design capacity in input volume, processing time or memory. It checks reliability and robustness, for example by simulating database transactions beyond expected capacity.

Suggested answers
Answer 1: I is input data, S is the program state at input, and R is the expected result.
Answer 2: Random pairs may all make the first value smaller and miss the defective second branch.
Answer 3: Black-box is functional testing; white-box is structural testing.
Answer 4: 0 and 1.
Answer 5: For num < 50 or num > 150, {49, 100} covers both branches; {49, 100, 200} also covers the component conditions.
Answer 6: A driver holds the non-local data used by the module under test; a stub is a dummy for a function the module calls.
Answer 7: It passes when ValueError is raised inside the context.
Answer 8: Write a failing test, implement enough to pass, then refactor while tests pass.
Answer 9: A function that always returns True would pass. Test non-primes and boundaries too.
Answer 10: To detect errors at module interfaces, including parameter passing and communication.
1. Which boundary values should be checked for isPrime(num)?
Answer: 0 and 1.
2. For min(x, y), which tests cover both branches?
Answer: (3, 8) returns 3 through the True branch; (9, 4) returns 4 through the False branch.
3. What do {49, 100, 200} establish for num < 50 or num > 150?
Answer: They achieve multiple condition coverage: the first component is True for 49, both are False for 100, and the second is True for 200.
4. What is the difference between a driver and a stub?
Answer: A driver holds the non-local data used by the module under test; a stub is a dummy for a function the module calls. Top down uses stubs; bottom up uses drivers.
5. When does pytest.raises(ValueError) pass?
Answer: It passes when ValueError is raised inside the context.
6. Why does replacing the count with 10 on the second addition fail?
Answer: After two additions of 10, the count should be 20. Replacement leaves 10.
7. What is the Red–Green–Refactor order?
Answer: Write a failing test, implement enough to pass, then refactor while tests pass.
8. Which integration strategy starts with lower-level modules?
Answer: Bottom up integration; drivers supply the non-local data required by the modules.
9. Distinguish smoke, performance and stress testing.
Answer: Smoke testing checks basic functionality before system testing. Performance testing checks non-functional requirements. Stress testing is a type of performance testing beyond design capacity.
10. How is cyclomatic complexity calculated here?
Answer: Number of decision and loop statements + 1 = 3 + 1 = 4; at least four test cases.
11. Why is one passing is_prime(5) test insufficient?
Answer: A function that always returns True would pass. Test non-primes and boundaries too.
